newsitem.title: UK: Advertising group Cordiant plans three-way split.
newsitem.headline: Advertising group Cordiant plans three-way split.

text.p: Advertising and marketing group Cordiant Plc, which has been in existence for only two years, said Monday it planned to split into three independently managed businesses, Saatchi & Saatchi, Bates and Zenith.
Cordiant said Saatchi & Saatchi and Bates, both international advertising agencies, will become publicly traded companies and they will jointly own Zenith, a media services group.

"This strategy is driven by the will to serve our clients better," Cordiant Chief Executive Bob Seelert, who will become CEO of Saatchi & Saatchi, said in a statement. "Demerger will energise the operators in the networks and unlock the considerable potential residing in our businesses."
Initial market reaction to the news was positive, with Cordiant shares adding 7 pence to 137 pence, valuing the company at about 600 million pounds ($980 million).
The group changed its name from Saatchi & Saatchi to Cordiant only two years ago, came during a period of upheaval when founders Maurice and Charles Saatchi left the company after a boardroom battle.
Their departure was followed by the loss of several other key company figures and important accounts, plunging the company into the red in 1995.
However, Seelert, an American, has since returned the group to profit and has spent much of the past 15 months reviewing the group and analysing how to unlock value for shareholders.

Cordiant said that separating Bates from Saatchi & Saatchi would remove client conflicts and enable both to pursue new business. Shares in each company will be traded on the London and New York stock exchanges.
Management estimates that the move will open up a further 10 percent of the world advertising market to Bates.
The group operates in 90 countries and employs more than 10,000 people and the split-up is expected to make the businesses more flexible and give staff clearer targets.
Cordiant also hopes that Zenith, which buys advertising space and plans campaigns, will be encouraged to recruit clients above and beyond those of its two parent agencies.
As a result of the split, Cordiant shareholders will own stock in two separately listed companies.

Details of the plan were expected to be sent to shareholders in September, prior to a vote at an extraordinary general meeting the following month. Separate dealings of the two new groups are expected in December.
